newsitem.title: UK: Madrid hopes euro will give it cheaper financing.
newsitem.headline: Madrid hopes euro will give it cheaper financing.

text.p: Madrid will refinance its debt at a cheaper rate when Spain adopts the euro and so will not issue any new bonds until the end of 1998, the president of the regional government of Madrid said on Monday.

"Interest rates are dropping and this will allow us to refinance public debt at a cheaper rate once we actually join the single currency," Alberto Ruiz Gallardon told Reuters after a presentation for investors in London.
"We will have the whole of 1998 to prepare for this," he said. "We will not be issuing any bonds until the end of 1998."

"We will be moving along in the direction of the convergence criteria laid down by Brussels," Gallardon said, adding market conditions should allow Madrid to lower its indebtedness, particularly its short-term debt.

Gallardon was leading a team including regional finance officials from Comunidad de Madrid aimed at encouraging investment in the region, which already has more direct foreign investment than any other region in Spain.
Gallardon said the convergence of Spanish government debt and German bunds was making money "cheaper" in Spain and would enable the city to refinance roughly 300 billion pesetas of public debt.

The premium for 10-year Spanish government bonds over their German equivalents was around 140 basis points today, from around 370 b.p. at the start of the year, reflecting market views that the extra risk of holding Spanish debt was declining.

The Spanish government's greatest ambition is to join EMU in its first stage, planned for January 1999. Considered a "Club Med" country -- along with Italy and Portugal -- Spain's low inflation has induced optimism about its prospects of joining EMU at the outset.
Gallardon said Madrid was looking for financing for new projects involving transport infrastructure and he will visit Paris, Frankfurt, Zurich and Milan this week.
"I would not like this visit to be seen as an isolated incident, but the first step towards a fluid, harmonious relationship in the long term," Gallardon told the gathering hosted by SBC Warburg.
